bridge.eyebrow: Introducing the HTML to JSON solution
bridge.title: From HTML/CSS to structured video.
bridge.description: Neonix compiles HTML/CSS into a structured JSON document — where every layer and property stays independently editable instead of becoming a flattened, unchangeable render. No-code designers can open and refine projects visually in the editor without touching code. It's what lets developers, designers, and AI agents collaborate transparently on the same document.

items.question: Why do I need cloud rendering if I can just render videos at home?
items.answer:
It's true — you can absolutely render videos at home using CapCut, Premiere, or traditional editing software for manual, one-off projects. But the equation changes completely once you're building Video-as-Code from HTML/CSS. You need dedicated cloud infrastructure to:

Avoid silent failures: If you write your own render scripts, you'll run into missing fonts, flaky network errors while loading assets, or animation timing drift. The result is batches of exported videos with missing visuals, missing audio, broken layouts, or frozen mid-render.

Fully free up your machine: Code-based video rendering is extremely RAM-, CPU-, and GPU-intensive. Render at home and your machine locks up, overheats, and can't do anything else. Cloud rendering carries that entire hardware burden in the cloud.

items.question: Why use Neonix's rendering service instead of setting up our own infrastructure on AWS/GCP?
items.answer: Building and optimizing your own render infrastructure takes significant trial-and-error and is easy to fall into hidden cost traps — egress bandwidth optimization, job queue configuration, hardware bottleneck handling. With over 5 years of hands-on experience operating cloud rendering systems, we've already solved these complex problems. You focus on your product and business — we carry the heavy lifting of hardware, speed, and cost optimization.

items.question: Does the infrastructure really auto-scale, or is that just marketing?
items.answer: Yes. The auto-scaling system reacts to the real render queue — when job volume spikes, compute expands automatically; when load drops, resources contract. No manual configuration or pre-provisioned capacity needed.

items.question: How is the 40–50% cost savings calculated?
items.answer: Compared to operating your own render infrastructure (buying/renting fixed servers, building your own transcoding pipeline), Neonix's automated pipeline eliminates idle compute costs and reduces manual operations headcount.

items.question: What happens if I render many videos at once?
items.answer: A queue-based architecture processes jobs asynchronously, so hundreds of jobs can queue and run in parallel without bottlenecking the system or slowing down any single job. For example, if you submit 10 render jobs, we dispatch 10 separate machines to render them in parallel — keeping both quality and turnaround time intact.

items.question: Is Neonix a good fit for a small startup or solo SaaS builder?
items.answer: Yes — this is exactly the customer segment we optimize cost for first. You pay based on actual usage, with no need to invest in fixed infrastructure the way a large enterprise would.

items.question: Is my data and video processed transparently?
items.answer: Yes. The entire transcoding/render pipeline is automated and traceable through a structured JSON document — there's no "black box" step you can't inspect.

items.question: Do I need to know how to code to use Neonix?
items.answer: Not required. Neonix's HTML/CSS-to-JSON compiler comes with a visual editor that lets people without coding skills design and edit videos. For developers or AI agents, the platform also supports integration through MCP and the API.
